notes.title: Proto Goblin Update
notes.notes:
Hello, headmasters and headmistresses of magic schools! :cutedragon:

It’s been a long time! Sorry for the long silence. Here’s a small balance and bug-fix update (see the non-exhaustive list at the bottom of this post). This is also a technical update, paving the way for a major expansion coming later this year. This expansion will allow us to deliver the final, definitive version of Spellcaster University.

This game has been a labor of love for us, but the time has come to move on to new video game projects. This expansion will let us wrap up the adventure properly.

A quick word as well for those who interacted with us throughout development: for the past two years, we’ve been very quiet. Various family reasons (and perhaps, paradoxically, a need to take a breather after the incredible reception Spellcaster University received—thank you again!) led us to gradually step back from communication, though not from development, which continued at a slower pace.

For a long time, we hesitated to create an expansion for Spellcaster University. We had plenty of ideas but feared overloading an already rich game. However, as time passed, we refined our vision and arrived at something we truly like. I’ll be sharing some visuals of what’s coming “soon.”

Balance:

[list]
[*]     The chance to gain the Heroic trait from the Heroic Statue increases from 3% to 4%.
[*]     Increases the efficiency of the Future Heating Boxes by 25%.
[*]     Increases the effects (both positive and negative) of the Tentacle artifact by 20%.
[*]     Doubles the effect of the Old-fashioned trait.
[*]     Doubles the effect of the Ugly trait.
[*]     Doubles the effect of the Aggressive trait.
[*]     Doubles the effect of the Unshakable trait.
[*]     Doubles the effect of the Resilient trait (outside of dungeons).
[*]     Doubles the effect of the Brave trait (outside of dungeons).
[*]     Increases the effect of the Green Dragon's Blessing by approximately 30%.
[*]     Increases the effect of the Blue Dragon's Blessing by approximately 30%.
[*]     Increases the effect of the Black Dragon's Blessing by approximately 30%.
[*]     Increases the effect of the Purple Dragon's Blessing by approximately 30%.
[*]     Increases the effect of the White Dragon's Blessing by approximately 30%.
[*]     Increases the effect of the Turquoise Dragon's Blessing by approximately 30%.
[*]     The Bloody Curse now accelerates reputation loss by 20% instead of 10%.
[/list]

Bug Fixes:

[list]
[*]     Fixed a bug that caused excessive CPU usage when displaying the in-game date.
[*]     The student information panel no longer briefly appears with incorrect stats before updating on the first frame.
[*]     In all languages (except French), fixed a missing space in the graduation ceremony text.
[*]     Reduced the risk of students getting stuck on certain maps (especially in the mountain and volcano).
[*]     General optimization by disabling unnecessary background debugging tools.
[/list]

notes.title: Major content update "Pegasus Rider"
notes.notes:
Hello all mages, witches and other demonists, :fatpegasus::fatpegasus::fatpegasus:

Today we made available a major new content update. We talked about it in terms of free DLC, but concretely everything is added directly into the game, you don't have to do anything.

To benefit from all the new features, it is better to start a new game. If you are in the middle of a campaign, most of the new features will only be available from the next level. The new features do not change the main mechanics, you may have to explore the decks to discover them.

The big new features are two new rooms with unique mechanics, fifteen new pieces of equipment and the cards that go with them. A new artifact and brand new futures as a bonus. I won't go into details, I'll let you discover. This is the biggest update since 1.0.

Two days ago we released a special update that introduces a series of small seasonal events spread throughout the year. We've also made some fixes, optimizations, and added some graphical variety to the castle balconies. It's a small update while waiting for the free DLC.

notes.title: End of early access now !
notes.notes:
This is the 1.00! The whole team would like to thank all the players who participated in the Spellcaster University early access. The game has evolved a lot in almost two years thanks to you. But this is not the end of the road. We will continue to work on Spellcaster University: in addition to the updates that will fix the inevitable bugs that will be reported to us, we will be releasing a free DLC in autumn that will focus on magic items and student equipment. And we have other ideas for the future. Thanks again to everyone!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33779302/ceca4d4adad20cec9666c8b09b90a7d0c6941156.png[/img]

New(major): Some events offer your students the opportunity to go on an expedition. Select your champions and guide them through the dungeons to collect loot. This brand new module includes spells, illustrations, specific events, and many other things.
New(major): New music, for days, nights and dungeons.
New: New variable objectives to renew your games.
New: Many new languages.
New: New events.
New: Display of the levels won on the global map.
New: Possibility to take back in hand the played artifacts.
New: The speed can now be controlled with the numeric keys.
New: Phoenix artifact boost dungeon expeditions.
New: Orc hound beat your students to motivate them.
New: New UI sounds.
New(major): Soundscapes for each region.
New: Barricaded doors for unused access to rooms (purely aesthetic).
New: Unique first names and surnames for each type of student.
New(major): Help book with a lot of information.
New: The stat book has been revamped, with more and more stats!
New: The general stat panel is accessible from the game.
New: New sounds for animations (like guinea pigs roaming the corridors).
New: New animations of injury and madness for students.
New: More equipment on the 2D portraits.
New: New 3D visual for graduating students. They no longer mysteriously disappear from your school.

Balance(major): Lots of adjustments on the effect of rooms, artifacts and equipment.
Balance: Some artifacts have a new effect that increases the efficiency of students in dungeons.
Balance: Some traits have a new effect that increases (or decrease !) the efficiency of students in dungeons.
Balance: The witch cat is now less effective (approximately 33% less effective).
Balance: Speed of advance of the evil adjusted to correspond to the modifications of the 1.0.
Balance: Resource quests are now more difficult.

Fix(major): Fixed a serious problem that made the game have a 1 in 5 million chance (precisely!) of crashing each time the random number generator was used.
Fix(major): Optimization of CPU consumption by reducing the number of operations performed in each cycle (such as unnecessary UI refresh).
Fix: Lots of various small fixes that we haven't seriously listed.
Fix: Pieces of equipment require at least one point in the magic involved to be equipped.
Fix: The Fir Ent card is now in the Nature deck rather than the base deck.
Fix: Changes in the advance of the forces of evil are now expressed as a percentage.
Fix: Organic rules now work as expected.
Fix: Full screen is not inverted anymore (it was a very stupid bug anyway...).
Fix: Forbidden characters on the different OS can no longer be used to name a school.
Fix: Improvement of the navmesh of the mountain level.
Fix: Easier (a bit) to place gazebo.
Fix: It is easier to select sleeping students (even if it is disrespectful to their sleep).

And a lot of other stuff that we didn't take the time to list in this changelog!

notes.title: Some news from Spellcaster University and the next 1.0
notes.notes:
Greetings to all magic school directors. Today we have a small announcement to let you know a few things about the immediate future of Spellcaster University.

The first thing we wanted to tell you is that the pace of updates is going to decrease significantly, because unless there are major bugs, the next update will be 1.0 and the release of early access. When will this final release take place? It is not yet fixed, but expect something between 2 and 4 months. We will announce a definitive date soon.

What does this mean for you, dear magic school directors? 
[list]
[*] new events
new languages (a priori we are targeting: Spanish, Polish, Korean, Japanese, German) in addition to those already available
*] a completely rewritten version of the English version
*] more improvements of UI
[*] and a big extra addition to enrich the gameplay. For now, here's just a little preview of what's coming... we'll keep the surprise for now.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33779302/ae001ea13d2ffc76c4f42eeaf6ff396c4b204e58.png[/img]
But what is it? What are these creatures? Well, let's say your students are going to have some extra work! But we'll talk about that later in detail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33779302/3041e2d6521d3214b7afa632b75710d25da2fb32.png[/img]
An improvement of the world map under development.

Finally, we would like to make it clear that the 1.0 release does not mean the end of Spellcaster University's development. We still have quite a few community-suggested improvements that we would like to add. Even though we won't be able to do "everything"! Thanks to all of you!

notes.title: Update 0.98 - Vengeful Archimage
notes.notes:
A new update with new content and gameplay additions ! We also integrate the Steam cloud. We've always tried to ensure backward compatibility of savegames, but adding the Steam Cloud can eventually lead to some problems. We have tried to anticipate all possible scenarios, but if this update should cause you to lose access to your savegames, do not hesitate to report it here https://github.com/JulienNigon/SpellcasterUniversity-Bug-Report/issues. We will do our best to help you recover them.

:fatpegasus: New: 8 new musics
:fatpegasus: New: 25 new futures: 5 per magical people (deep-ones, elves, vampires, werewolves and half-orcs)
:fatpegasus: New: 7 new traits for teachers (former adventurer, love his job, learned...)
:fatpegasus: New: Steam Cloud for saved games
:fatpegasus: New: Levels of reputations with the factions granting you various bonuses and maluses.
:fatpegasus: New: Manywings artifact, a weird creature very useful for alchemy.
***
* Balance: event of the visit to the peasants rebalanced.
* Balance: "Skull" artifact is half as effective now.
* Balance: conditions to obtain a ghoul modified (because similar to the marionetist).
* Balance: the acceleration factor of the evil beyond the normal time of a gameis increased from 280% to 380%. This means that if your game lasted twice as long as the "normal" time, the evil is moving at 380% of its normal speed.
***
* Fix: the "Demanding" trait now works correctly.
* Fix: the curves in the statistics book no longer go completely out of whack when a save is resumed.
* Fix: it is no longer possible to accumulate several pieces of equipment on the same location (e.g. several staffs, several medallions, etc...)
* Fix: when loading a save the students appear directly with their equipment.
* Fix: the thaumaturges do not make any more mana with each recruitment of a new student.
* Fix: the belvedere can be placed in mirror.
* Fix: typos and ressources logo not showing when needed.

notes.title: Build your own Hogwarts-style magic school in this charming management sim
notes.notes:
I'm not a Harry Potter fan but I do love the concept of Hogwarts, a fantastical school where children can learn powerful magical spells and be exposed to unthinkable evil due to the utter irresponsibility of the faculty. Spellcaster University, now in Early Access on Steam, lets you build and run your own version of a delightful yet dangerously deadly magic school.

The gameplay trailer above will give you a little look at how it all works and just how darn charming the art and animation is. Spellcaster University is a management sim—you construct a school, recruit students, hire faculty, and manage your budget and relationships with the rest of the realm, which include factions like orcs, dwarves, merchants, and adventurers.

But it's also part card game that runs on mana and money. There are six decks of cards to draw from representing five magical disciplines plus a base deck that runs on gold. Drawing from any deck gives you a choice of three cards that you'll use to build your school, one room at a time, staff classrooms with teachers, and add relics that provide various buffs and effects. Like, say, a magical bed with teeth that chews on students while they sleep! (More on that in a minute.)

There's also a ticking clock: The Lord of Evil is growing his power in a nearby graveyard and it's only a matter of time before he rises up and destroys your lovely, dangerous little school. Because every Hogwarts has its Voldemort.

As you cobble together your university with cards, events periodically occur forcing you to make decisions that will shape your game. Most of these have to do with other factions. The neighboring orcs are hungry, for example, and now they're banging on your door. Maybe you've already drawn an enchanted wafflemaker card from the deck and placed it in the school, so you can feed them some waffles to make them happy. Or you can suggest they go eat some nearby villagers (whose disposition toward you will plummet, naturally). Maybe you tell them to scram, and they will—though if you keep sending them away with nothing, they'll eventually go on a rampage through your school. Hey, they're orcs. That's what they do.

The cards your draw will also let you choose what sort of headmaster you want to be. Are you the type of dean who adds a Child-Eater Bed to the dorms? It's a bed with huge, sharp teeth that will snack on your students while they sleep. It may affect your student's health negatively (surprise!) but it may generate an alchemical ingredient card you can use to craft potions. It's one of those moral dilemmas educators face every day in any school system.

One of the most enjoyable parts of Spellcaster University is zooming in close to see what's happening inside all the rooms you've built. You can watch students attend class (the assassin study room is my favorite, as you'll see your kids practicing stealthy movement and stabbing a practice dummy in a bed) and see your relics in action (if you acquire a little dragon, you can watch it flap its way through the school). If you're teaching classes about portal magic or alchemy you'll see experiments (and disasters) taking place. If the orcs or the undead raid, you can watch your students and teachers battle them. Unhappy students will tag rooms with graffiti, which is why it's important to institute some sort of discipline—like a jail cell or chains and shackles. It's for their own good, probably.

As years pass and your school grows, some of your students will graduate which can add to your school's reputation (or hurt it, if the learning environment was so poor it led to kids becoming peasants instead of mages). And eventually, the Lord of Evil will arrive to destroy your university and you'll need to rebuild in a new location—such as inside a volcano, where you'll meet some dwarves living under the mountain, or along the coast where a pirate faction will have to be dealt with.

You can try to delay the Lord of Evil's attack as you play by meeting with him and trying to raise his disposition—but that's difficult since he's, you know, evil. I haven't completed the game yet, but it sounds like there's a final showdown where your students have hopefully become powerful enough to face the Lord of Evil instead of just fleeing to a new location.

Spellcaster University is currently in Early Access so there are some bugs here and there—sometimes teachers get stuck in doorways, preventing a class from starting (saving and reloading seems to fix it). I've also had a few crashes to desktop, so make sure you save your game regularly since there doesn't appear to be an autosave system in place.

But bugs aside it's charming as hell, and there's a nice amount of depth in the traits of your students and teachers—each have personalities and alignments that make them ideal for certain magical disciplines and less so for others. The RNG of the card system and randomized students and faculty makes each school you build a bit different, and the dynamic way the rooms click into place always results in a weird and wondrous looking university. 

Until the Lord of Evil shows up, that is, and you have to rebuild. On the plus side, maybe this time you'll get construct it on the back of a giant sea turtle.
